deep.reconstruction:
There are no calculations on this page. It holds several drafts, in Latin and German, of a single problem statement. Riemann rewrites and corrects the wording repeatedly, as you would for a prize question or exercise.

Draft 1 (Latin): 'Datis duobus cylindris infinitis inter se parallelis, perfecte electricitatem conducentibus et penitus isolatis, determinatur distributio electricitatis in statu aequilibrii & vires in punctum quodvis positionis exercitae, pro nonnullis formis basium.' In English: given two infinite, mutually parallel cylinders that conduct electricity perfectly and are completely insulated, determine the equilibrium distribution of electricity and the forces it exerts on any point, for some shapes of the cross-section.

Draft 2 (German, headed 'Die Vertheilung der Electr.'): 'Es soll die Vertheilung der Electricität [auf] zweier unendlicher einander parallelen Cylinder, von denen angenommen werden [soll] dass sie vollkommene Leiter der Electricität und vollkommen isolirt sind ... Es sollen für einige [einfache] Formen des Querschnitts die Vertheilung der Electricität im Gleichgewicht und die von ihr in einem Punkt ausgeübten Kräfte bestimmt werden.' The content is the same as draft 1.

Draft 3 (Latin, the most finished): 'Duo cylindri infiniti inter se paralleli electricitatem perfecte conducentes et penitus isolati quantitatibus datis electricitatis pro unitate longitudinis repleantur; quaeritur quae sit distributio electricitatis in statu aequilibrii et quales vires in punctum quodvis exerceat.' In English: two such cylinders are charged with given quantities of electricity per unit length; find the equilibrium distribution and the force at an arbitrary point. A clause restricting this to 'aliquot formis regularibus basium' (some regular cross-sections) and a sentence 'Postulatur solutio hujus problematis' are struck out.

Modern formulation (my addition, not on the page). Work in the plane of the cross-section. Find a potential V(x,y) such that:
- ΔV = 0 outside the two cross-sections D1 and D2;
- V = c1 on ∂D1 and V = c2 on ∂D2, both constants;
- V ~ -2(e1+e2) log r + O(1) at infinity (Gaussian units, line charges e_i per unit length);
- the flux through each boundary gives the charge on it: -(1/4π)∮_{∂Di} ∂V/∂n ds = e_i.

The surface density is σ = -(1/4π) ∂V/∂n, and the force on a unit charge is -∇V.

This is a planar Dirichlet problem on a doubly connected region. Its natural method is conformal mapping onto an annulus, or the use of a complex potential. Riemann's posthumous fragment on conductors with circular cross-section and parallel axes, which deals with conformal mapping of circle-bounded figures, treats exactly this.

For two circular sections (my addition), take radii a and b with centre distance d. In bipolar coordinates the equipotentials are Apollonius circles of two line charges ±e placed at the limiting points ±c. There V = -2e log(|z-c|/|z+c|) + const. The capacitance per unit length is 1/(2 arccosh((d²-a²-b²)/(2ab))) in Gaussian units.

The page contains no derivation. The circular-case material above is context added for orientation.
errors: There are no mathematical steps to check.
Linguistic slips in the draft: 'determinatur' should be 'determinetur' or 'determinentur' in a question formulation, and 'vires ... exercitae' should be 'exercitas'.
German slip: 'die Vertheilung ... zweier ... Cylinder' leaves the governing preposition ambiguous ('auf zwei ... Cylindern').

results.what: Formulation of the equilibrium problem for charge on two infinite, parallel, perfectly conducting, insulated cylinders with given charge per unit length. This is a 2D Dirichlet problem on a doubly connected domain, posed for several cross-section shapes.
results.modern_name: Two-conductor electrostatic problem in the plane; capacitance of parallel cylinders; Dirichlet problem for doubly connected domains (solvable via conformal mapping onto an annulus, or bipolar coordinates for circles)
results.usually_credited_to: Circular case: Kelvin (W. Thomson), method of images, 1840s; Maxwell, Treatise (1873); bipolar coordinates. General conformal-map approach: Riemann's school; later Schottky (1877) for multiply connected domains.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a problem statement, apparently a draft of a prize question or exercise, with no solution on the page. Riemann's interest in electricity on parallel cylinders, and in conformal mapping of figures bounded by circles, is already documented through the fragment published in his Werke. The page's wording, including its multilingual drafts, adds only minor archival detail.

checkable.asserts: The logarithmic potential of a line charge is harmonic in the plane away from the axis. Expected result: 0.

checkable.asserts: The level sets |z-c|/|z+c| = k of the two-line-charge potential are circles (Apollonius circles), so they can serve as conductor surfaces for circular cylinders. Expected result: 0.
Capacitance per unit length (Gaussian units) of two parallel circular cylinders with radii a and b and centre distance d.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck word before 'perfecte' appears to be 'qui', and 'in statu aequilibrii' is an interlinear insertion placed above 'vires' in line 2, not in line 1.
'repleantur' (not 'replantur'). The interlinear insertion reads approximately 'pro unitate longitudinis dati repleantur', with 'quantitatibus datis' intended.

German: 'zweier unendlichen einander parallelen Cylinder'. The struck word after 'Es soll die Vertheilung der Electricitaet' is likely 'auf', and the insertion reads 'von denen angenommen werden [soll] dass sie'.
The struck word before 'Formen des Querschnitts' is possibly 'einfache' or 'einfachere'.
'nonnullis' is written above the struck 'qui aliquot' in the line 'pro ... formis basium'.
The struck word before 'exerceat' is uncertain ('formabis' is doubtful; possibly 'formarum').
